text:
lena: quick recap from today's arch sync — proposing a 'broker' pattern to unify hosted/dedicated/private routing without a persistent per-tenant sidecar. idea is a lightweight broker proxy that performs capability negotiation and auth handoff, then streams to the chosen runtime. would like feedback on failure modes and rollout strategy.

omar: curious — how is tenant isolation guaranteed if we remove sidecars? is the broker multitenant or per-az per-tenant?

lena: broker is multitenant but intentionally minimal: it only handles manifest validation, capability handshakes, and short-lived leasing to a runtime. isolation stays at the runtime (dedicated pools / private sidecars) and network policies. broker never touches model payloads/persistent secrets.

priya: so keys and secrets still live in the runtime's KMS/HSM and the broker only routes an ephemeral token? :+1:

lena: exactly. broker issues short-lived runtime tokens (30s-5m TTL) after it verifies manifest & tenant policy. runtime validates token with control-plane verifier. broker stores no long-term secrets.

maria: what about observability? we need token-level traces to correlate request -> runtime. can broker add trace headers without leaking PII?

lena: plan: broker injects opaquetrace-id header. control plane and runtime map it to tenant ID in telemetry backends with ACLs. broker can optionally redact at ingress.

tj: failure cases: if broker is down, hosted customers shouldn't be blocked. fallback idea: SDKs can fall back to direct-runtime endpoints when a tenant has pinned dedicated/private. is that what you're thinking?

lena: yes — fallback paths: 1) client-side pin to runtime (preferred for Dedicated/Private), 2) control-plane remote-proxy (current hosted flow), 3) broker-mediated route. Broker adds a circuit-breaker and will short-circuit to a degraded-but-available model variant in overload.

omar: any changes to the manifest shape? we should avoid adding more fields that private deploys must implement. maybe introduce a small 'hosting.handoff' object scoped to hosted-only defaults.

priya: sample manifest snippet suggestion:

```json
{"service": "llm-inference",
 "model": "gpt-open-13b",
 "hosting": {"handoff": {"prefer": ["broker","direct"], "max_ttl_s": 300}}
}
```

priya: keeps it optional so private deployments ignore it.

maria: rollout ops question — can we canary the broker per-region and opt tenants in? we need a way to opt out per-tenant if issues appear.

lena: yes, control-plane will have an opt-in metadata tag and we can add a feature-flag gate. plan: start with small PLG cohort, enable observability hooks, then open to dedicated customers.

tj: security note — broker must authenticate to control-plane and runtime. recommend mTLS for all broker -> runtime traffic and short-lived JWT for client SDK -> broker. Also add token reuse detection telemetry.

omar: performance — added latency of broker hop is the big concern for low-latency apps. can the broker operate in "fast-pass" mode where it only performs header negotiation and then establishes a direct TCP/stream tunnel to runtime to avoid per-request proxying?

lena: yes. architecture includes two modes: negotiate-and-proxy (for auditing, inspection) and negotiate-and-tunnel (fast path). default to tunnel for latency-sensitive routes.

priya: +1. we should preserve metrics to attribute cost to hosted vs dedicated even when tunneling. need billing hook in the handshake.

lena: noted — handshake will attach billing metadata and route decision reason. role of broker in billing will be purely attribution, not metering tokens.

infra-bot: deploy-checklist created: https://infra/repo/PR/4287 — includes mTLS cert rotation, canary plan, feature flag, and telemetry panel templates.

maria: last thing — testing matrix: 1) latency microbench with tunnel vs proxy, 2) failover to direct runtime when broker unhealthy, 3) credential rotation during active streams. i'll own the testing harness.

lena: awesome — i'll write up a short RFC with sequence diagrams and the manifest extension draft. we should converge on naming (broker vs broker-proxy). thanks all for quick feedback :rocket:
